st.2: The main domesticated animals were humped cattle, sheep and goats.

st.4: According to the Mahabharata, the Andhras fought on the side of the Pandavas.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: in the Mahabharata the Andhras fought on the side of the Kauravas.

st.2: The Purusha Sukta belongs to the tenth Mandala, a later addition to the Rigveda.

x: Both statements are correct: varna first appears in the Rigveda, and the Purusha Sukta is in the tenth Mandala, a late addition, not in the oldest family books.

st.3: PGW was first found at Hastinapur in the excavations of 1940–44.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: PGW was first found at Ahichchhatra in 1940–44; Hastinapur was dug later by B.B. Lal.

st.3: In Satavahana Andhra the offspring of an anuloma union were called Chandala.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: anuloma offspring were called Ugra; Chandala was the term for pratiloma offspring.

st.2: The Somapura Mahavihara at Paharpur was built by Dharmapala.

x: All three statements are correct: Vikramashila became the main centre after Nalanda, Somapura Mahavihara at Paharpur was built by Dharmapala (Gopala founded Odantapuri), and Dharmapala had Haribhadra in his court.

st.2: Vajrayana ritualism strengthened Buddhism against decline.
st.4: Hiuen Tsang found Sriparvata flourishing under royal patronage.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Vajrayana ritualism was one of the causes of decline. Statement 4 is wrong: Hiuen Tsang found Sriparvata without patronage.

st.2: Seleucus did not cede Bactria.
st.4: Chandragupta's daughter was married to Seleucus.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Seleucus ceded Aria, Arachosia, Paropanisadai and Gedrosia but not Bactria, and received 500 elephants. Statement 4 is wrong: the marriage alliance went the other way, a Seleucid princess being given to Chandragupta.

st.2: Four Kanva kings ruled.
st.3: The last Kanva, Susharman, was overthrown by Menander.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Vasudeva killed Devabhuti, and four Kanva kings ruled (c. 73–28 BC). Statement 3 is wrong: Susharman was overthrown by the Satavahanas, not Menander.

st.2: He sent an army west only after an alliance with Satakarni.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Kharavela sent an army west ignoring Satakarni, not in alliance with him.

st.2: Ashoka gave the Barabar caves to the Ajivikas.

x: All three statements are correct: the caves are in Jehanabad and cut in granite, Ashoka gave the Barabar caves to the Ajivikas, and Dasaratha gave the Nagarjuni caves.

st.4: Kumaragupta I bore the title Mahendraditya.

x: All four statements are correct: Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha were only Maharajas, Samudragupta was Prithivyama Pratiratha and Smith's 'Napoleon of India', and Kumaragupta I was Mahendraditya (Vikramaditya was Chandragupta II).

st.4: Ramagupta ruled immediately after Chandragupta II.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: Ramagupta ruled before Chandragupta II, who killed him and took the throne.

st.2: The head of a guild was called the Sarthavaha.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Sarthavaha was the caravan leader (chief merchant); the guild head was the Jyeshthaka (Pramukha).

st.4: His rival Nasiruddin Qabacha held Multan and Uch.

x: All four statements are correct: tanka and jital, investiture in 1229, Yildiz defeated at Tarain in 1216, and Qabacha's base was Multan and Uch (Badaun was Iltutmish's own early iqta).

st.4: The southern kingdoms were annexed and made provinces.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: in the south Alauddin sought wealth and tribute, the kings kept their thrones; only the north was annexed.

st.2: Rajon ki Baoli at Mehrauli was built in 1506 in the reign of Sikandar Lodi.
st.3: When Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in 1498, Vijayanagara was ruled by Deva Raya II.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: Rajon ki Baoli (1506) belongs to Sikandar Lodi's reign. Statement 3 is wrong: in 1498 Vijayanagara was under Immadi Narasimha (Saluva); Deva Raya II died in 1446.

st.1: Criminal law followed the sharia alone.
st.3: The organisation of the army in decimal units was a Perso-Arabic element of the government.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: criminal law followed the Sultan's rules (zawabit). Statement 3 is wrong: the decimal army was a Turko-Mongol element.

st.3: Amir Khusrau wrote the Padmavat.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Padmavat was written by Malik Muhammad Jayasi, not Amir Khusrau.

st.2: He wrote his works under the patronage of Alauddin Khalji.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Barani wrote his Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and Fatawa-i-Jahandari under Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

st.3: Babur took the title 'Ghazi' after the Battle of Chanderi.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Babur took the title 'Ghazi' after Khanwa (1527).

st.2: The Ibadat Khana, built in 1575, was opened to Hindus, Jains, Christians and Zoroastrians only in 1578.

x: All three statements are correct: the pilgrimage tax and jizya went in 1563 and 1564, the Ibadat Khana (1575) was at first for Muslims and was thrown open to other faiths in 1578, and Shaikh Mubarak drafted the Mahzar.

st.3: Du-aspa sih-aspa was first granted to Mahabat Khan by Akbar.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: du-aspa sih-aspa was introduced by Jahangir, first for Mahabat Khan.

st.3: The Dal Khalsa, the combined force of the misls, was organised by Bhai Mani Singh.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Dal Khalsa was organised by Kapur Singh; Bhai Mani Singh healed the Bandai-Tat Khalsa split.

st.3: Its architect Ata-ullah was the son of Ustad Isa.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Ata-ullah was the son of Ustad Ahmad Lahori.

st.1: Under Shivaji the Hon was a gold coin and the Shivrai a copper coin.

x: All three statements are correct: the Hon was gold and the Shivrai copper, the Rajvyavahar Kosh replaced Persian terms with Sanskrit ones, and Ganimi Kava was guerrilla warfare.

st.1: Hyderabad was founded in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.

x: All three statements are correct: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah founded Hyderabad in 1591, Machilipatnam drew Europeans for chintz and diamonds, and Marco Polo visited Motupalli.

st.3: Permission for the first English factory at Machilipatnam was given by the Golconda Sultan Abdullah Qutb Shah.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the permission came from Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.

st.2: It was later cited as evidence of a common Hindu-Muslim struggle against British rule.

x: Both statements are correct: the joint Hindu-Muslim fight of 1857 was later cited as proof of a shared struggle and against the two-nation theory.

st.3: Indians were excluded from the artillery, which was kept in European hands.
st.4: Recruitment shifted to Awadh, Bihar and Central India.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the artillery was kept with Europeans. Statement 4 is wrong: recruitment shifted away from Awadh, Bihar and Central India to the 'martial races' of Punjab, Nepal and NWFP.

st.3: The attack on the Residency was repulsed by Col. Davidson.

x: All three statements are correct: the Wahabi conspiracy (1839) fell under Nasir-ud-Daula, Turrebaz Khan attacked on 17 July 1857, and the attack was repulsed by Col. Davidson.

st.2: The Labour Swaraj Party was formed at Calcutta in 1925.
st.4: The All-India Workers and Peasants Party (1928) called for a boycott of the Congress.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the Labour Swaraj Party was formed at Calcutta (1925). Statement 4 is wrong: the WPP sought to make the Congress more revolutionary, not to boycott it.

st.3: The Brahmo Trinity of Andhra was Veeresalingam, Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu and Desiraju Peda Bapayya.

x: All three statements are correct: the first Prarthana Samaj was at Rajahmundry (1878), Mannava Butchaiah Pantulu edited the Hindu Reformer, and the Brahmo Trinity was Veeresalingam, Venkataratnam Naidu and Desiraju Peda Bapayya.

st.3: Bismarck's 'blood and iron' speech of 1862 relates to the unification of Germany.

x: All three statements are correct: Panikkar's view on unification, English as a link language, and Bismarck's speech relates to German unification.

st.3: R.C. Dutt was the author of 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901).

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' was written by Dadabhai Naoroji; Dutt wrote 'The Economic History of India'.

st.4: It was annulled at the Delhi Durbar of 1911, when Lord Minto was Viceroy.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Viceroy at the annulment (1911) was Lord Hardinge II.

st.2: Bipin Chandra Pal was deported to Mandalay in 1907.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it was Lajpat Rai (with Ajit Singh) who was deported to Mandalay in 1907; Pal was jailed for refusing to testify against Aurobindo.

st.3: The Commonwealth of India Bill demanded Dominion Status for India.

x: All four statements are correct: Besant renamed the Madras Standard New India, Lansbury introduced the Bill, which sought Dominion Status (not complete independence), and its Article 7 listed seven rights.

st.2: Mahadev Desai and Narhari Parikh assisted Gandhi in the Champaran inquiry.

x: All three statements are correct: Rajkumar Shukla brought Gandhi, Mahadev Desai and Narhari Parikh were among his helpers (not planters' leaders), and Gandhi reached Champaran on 10 April 1917.

st.4: foreshadowed only the Fundamental Rights, and none of the Directive Principles, of the present Constitution.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Karachi resolution foreshadowed both Part III (Fundamental Rights) and Part IV (Directive Principles).

st.4: The INA did not surrender even after Japan's surrender of 15 August 1945.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the INA surrendered along with Japan on 15 August 1945.

st.2: Jinnah rejected the C.R. Formula.
st.4: The League raised the slogan 'Divide and Quit' at its Lahore session of 1940.

x: All three statements are correct: Sambamurthy backed the 1920 boycott, signed the Sribagh Pact, and became Speaker of the Madras Assembly in 1937 (not a Minister).

st.3: Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi was arrested at Vedaranyam.

x: All three statements are correct: Yerneni Subrahmanyam was the Telugu Dandi marcher, Durgabai led women at the Madras beach, and Rukmini Lakshmipathi was arrested at Vedaranyam.

st.1: The Nehru Report (1928) supported the idea of linguistic provinces.

x: All three statements are correct: the Nehru Report supported linguistic provinces, the Montford Report made no provision for Andhra, and Nagpur 1920 reorganised the PCCs on linguistic lines.

st.4: The Legislative Council was revived in 2007.

x: All four statements are correct: the Congress had 159 seats, 1957 polls were held only in Telangana, the Council of 1958 was abolished by NTR in 1985, and it was revived in 2007.

st.3: Under the Nizam's rules a person became a Mulki only by birth in Hyderabad State.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: a person could also become a Mulki by 15 years' continuous residence, not by birth alone.

st.3: The Greater Rayalaseema demand raised during bifurcation was not accepted in the 2014 Act.

x: All three statements are correct: the Hillmen's Association sought separation in 1907, Ghisingh founded the GNLF in 1980, and the Greater Rayalaseema demand found no place in the 2014 Act.

st.3: At Karivalamvanthanallur (Tenkasi) the Microlithic was followed directly by the Iron Age, with no Neolithic or Chalcolithic phase.

x: All three statements are correct: Mayiladumparai gives iron at 2172 BCE, Panayal is in Kasaragod, and Karivalamvanthanallur passed straight from the Microlithic to the Iron Age with no Chalcolithic phase.

st.2: The monks' cells of a vihara are arranged round a central hall called the Madhyashala.

x: All three statements are correct: the chaitya ends in an apse with a horseshoe window, the vihara's cells surround a central hall (Madhyashala, not the Garbhagriha of a temple), and uposatha was held there every 15 days.

st.3: He issued the first Sanskrit inscriptions in the Telugu lands.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the first Sanskrit inscriptions are credited to Ehuvala Santamula, the third Ikshvaku king, not the founder.

st.2: Bhaga was a tax of one-sixth of the produce.

x: All three statements are correct: the Gulmika guarded the borders, Bhaga was the king's one-sixth share of produce, and Vishti was forced labour (vetti).

st.2: They were carved from the bottom up, so the ground floor is the most finely finished.
st.4: They were first used by Buddhist monks and later became a Jain abode.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the caves were carved top-down, so the upper levels are finest and the ground floor crude. Statement 4 is wrong: the order is reversed; they were first a Jain abode and later used by Buddhists.

st.2: Manyakheta (Malkhed) is in present-day Karnataka.

x: All three statements are correct: Amoghavarsha I built Manyakheta, which is Malkhed in Kalaburagi district of Karnataka, and Elapura (Ellora) was the early seat.

st.3: They were first feudatories of the Pallavas and later of the Badami Chalukyas.

x: All four statements are correct: the Renati Cholas claimed Karikala's line, Renadu was Saptasahasra, they were early Pallava feudatories who later served the Badami Chalukyas, and the Banas and Vaidumbas followed them.

st.1: The Nandampudi agrahara was granted to Nannaya.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Nandampudi agrahara went to Narayana Bhattu; Nannaya only composed the grant.

st.2: The Dakshinatya (southern Nayaka) age covers the 17th and 18th centuries.

x: All three statements are correct: the Shiva Kavi Yugam is 1060-1260, the Dakshinatya age of the southern Nayaka courts is the 17th-18th centuries, and Appayacharya wrote Jinendra Kalyanabhyudayamu.

st.2: Ambadeva's victories are recorded in the Tripurantakam inscription.

x: All three statements are correct: Ambadeva headed Kadapa from 1272, his victories are in the Tripurantakam inscription (Chandupatla records Rudrama's death), and Nellore passed to the Pandyas after Muttukur.

st.4: Anavota, the first ruler of the division, was the son of Kumaragiri Reddi.

x: All four statements are correct: Kataya Vema died at Kakaraparthi (1414), Allada Reddi was regent, Vema (Veda) Reddi ruled de facto 1423-48, and the division was first under Kumaragiri's son Anavota.

st.2: After the battle George Russell took charge of the Vizianagaram forts.

x: All three statements are correct: Vizianagaram was sequestered in 1793, George Russell took charge of the forts, and Narayana Babu succeeded his slain father.

st.1: Raja Venkatappa Nayaka rose against the British at Shorapur (Surapur) in 1858.

x: All three statements are correct: Venkatappa Nayaka's rising was at Shorapur, Afzal-ud-Daula kept Salar Jung I as Diwan, and the 1st Cavalry was disarmed at Aurangabad.

st.2: Revenue was collected in cash.

x: Both statements are correct: the Collector combined revenue, magisterial and police powers, and the revenue was collected in cash.

st.2: The Buckingham Canal is a salt-water navigation canal running parallel to the Coromandel coast.

x: All three statements are correct: the railways tied the interior to Madras, the Buckingham Canal is a salt-water coastal canal (not through Kolleru), and it was extended in 1876-78 and is in NW-4.

st.1: William Carey's first printed Telugu Bible was produced at Serampore.

x: All three statements are correct: Carey printed the Telugu Bible at Serampore, Vartamana Tarangini was started by Sayyad Rahamtulla, and Kokkonda Venkataratnam was the first Andhra Mahamahopadhyaya.

st.3: Ranga joined the freedom struggle in 1930 on the call of Gandhi.

x: All four statements are correct: Ranga was Rythu Bandhu, ran Praja Bandhu and Navayuga, joined the struggle in 1930 on Gandhi's call (not Bose's), and the Kisan movement sought MSP and zamindari abolition.

st.4: Under Vijayanagara it mainly entertained the royal court, while Tolu Bommalata entertained the rural people.

x: All four statements are correct: the Jakkulas performed it, Koravanji was its precursor, Sugreeva Vijayam was the first published one, and under Vijayanagara it was a court art while Tolu Bommalata served rural Andhra.

st.3: During Seethala Panduga, Seethala Mata is worshipped as a guard against cholera.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the foundation stone (20 November 1951) was laid by President Rajendra Prasad.

st.1: He was placed on the throne as a boy of twelve by the Pallava ministers, nobles and people.

x: All three statements are correct: Nandivarman II was chosen as a boy of twelve by the ministers and nobles (Vikramaditya II was his enemy), was a contemporary of Tirumangai Alvar, and bore the title Pallavamalla.

st.3: The National Integration Council is a statutory body set up under an Act of Parliament.
st.4: Under Article 350-B the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is appointed by the Governor of each State.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the NIC is a non-statutory body set up by executive decision. Statement 4 is wrong: the Special Officer under Article 350-B is appointed by the President.

st.2: Uttarakhand's UCC, in force since 27 January 2025, makes the registration of live-in relationships optional.
st.3: In 2026 Amit Shah said that a UCC would cover all States and Union Territories by 2029.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Uttarakhand's UCC makes registration of live-in relationships mandatory. Statement 3 is wrong: Amit Shah spoke of the 21 NDA States, not all States and UTs.

st.1: The Untouchability (Offences) Act, an example of law as a factor of change, was renamed the SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act in 1976.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 was renamed the Protection of Civil Rights Act in 1976; the Atrocities Act is a separate law of 1989.

st.1: It must have a population of at least 10,000.
st.2: At least 75% of its main workers, male and female together, must be in non-farm work.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the threshold is 5,000. Statement 2 is wrong: the 75% non-farm test applies to male main workers only.

st.1: The Indian Succession Act, 1925 applies mainly to Muslims.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Indian Succession Act applies mainly to Christians, Parsis and others; Muslims follow their personal law.

st.2: Family Courts are set up by the Union Government under the Family Courts Act.
st.3: India's first exclusive women's court was set up at Delhi in 2013.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Family Courts are set up by the State Governments in consultation with the High Court (953 by July 2025). Statement 3 is wrong: the first women's court was at Malda, West Bengal.

st.2: Phule started the first girls' school in Bombay in 1848.
st.3: Phule was given the title 'Mahatma' by Mahatma Gandhi.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Phule's first girls' school (1848) was in Pune. Statement 3 is wrong: the title 'Mahatma' was given to Phule in 1888 by Vithalrao Wandekar, long before Gandhi.

st.2: The Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution was moved by Muhammad Ali Jinnah.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Lahore Resolution (adopted 24 March 1940) was moved by A.K. Fazlul Huq.

st.2: Pattabhi Sitaramayya was one of its members.

st.2: Most of them were main workers.
st.3: Bihar had the largest number of child labourers.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: only about 4.35 million were main workers; most were marginal workers. Statement 3 is wrong: Uttar Pradesh had the largest number.

st.2: The split system combines policy-making and implementation in the Secretariat.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the split system separates policy-making in the Secretariat from implementation by the executive departments.

st.2: Taneti Vanitha has been the Minister for Women and Child Welfare since 12 June 2024.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: since June 2024 the Women and Child Welfare Minister is Gummadi Sandhya Rani; Taneti Vanitha was Home Minister in the earlier government.

st.3: It is run by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
st.4: Garima Greh under SMILE are skill-training centres for transgender persons.

st.2: It provides PF, EPS pension and EDLI insurance.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: PF, EPS and EDLI are EPFO schemes; ESI gives medical, sickness, maternity and disablement benefits.

st.1: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs was formed in 2017 by splitting the Ministry of Urban Development.
st.3: PM SVANidhi gives street vendors working-capital loans only against collateral.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: MoHUA was formed by merging the two ministries, not by splitting one. Statement 3 is wrong: PM SVANidhi loans are collateral-free.

st.2: Of the 53 atrocity-prone villages listed by the MHA (July 2022), most are in Kadapa district.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: 47 of the 53 villages are in East Godavari; Kadapa has only 5.

st.2: BECA concerns encrypted communications data and equipment.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: BECA concerns the sharing of geospatial intelligence; encrypted communications is COMCASA.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: quotas do not fix exchange rates; they decide contributions, access to finance and votes.

st.3: A no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers can be moved in either House.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it is the Rajya Sabha that must return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha within 14 days. Statement 3 is wrong: a no-confidence motion can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.

st.4: The Secretary-General of each House is appointed by the President and holds the rank of Cabinet Secretary.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Lok Sabha Secretariat works under the Speaker, independent of the executive. Statement 4 is wrong: the Secretary-General is appointed by the presiding officer of the House.

st.2: The Chairman of the Estimates Committee is, by convention, appointed from the Opposition.
st.3: The Committee on Petitions is one of the three financial committees of Parliament.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the convention of an Opposition chairman applies to the Public Accounts Committee. Statement 3 is wrong: the three financial committees are PAC, Estimates and Public Undertakings.

st.1: The Governor is the Chancellor of the Central universities located in the State.
st.3: The Governor's report recommending President's Rule is made under Article 360.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Governor is Chancellor of the State universities; the President is Visitor of Central universities. Statement 3 is wrong: the report is made under Article 356; Article 360 is the financial emergency.
Both statements are correct: under Article 356 President's Rule may be imposed on the Governor's report or otherwise, and Article 365 makes non-compliance with Union directions a ground.

st.3: The Assembly may be dissolved before Parliament approves the proclamation.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: under Bommai the Assembly may only be kept in suspended animation; it can be dissolved only after Parliament approves the proclamation.

st.1: It was set up under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the NGT was set up under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 and became operational on 18 October 2010.

st.1: The Governor of a State is appointed by the President under Article 163.
st.2: Officers of the All India Services are recruited through the State Public Service Commissions.
st.3: An amendment affecting the federal structure needs ratification by half of the State Legislatures, each by a special majority.

x: Statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Governor is appointed under Articles 155-156; Article 163 is about the Council of Ministers. Statement 2 is wrong: AIS officers are recruited through the UPSC. Statement 3 is wrong: ratification by half the States needs only a simple majority in each.

st.2: Articles 19 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency.
st.3: Article 19 is suspended automatically in a National Emergency declared on any ground, including armed rebellion.
st.4: The 42nd Amendment barred judicial review of a proclamation of Emergency.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the protected Articles are 20 and 21, not 19. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 19 is suspended automatically only for war or external aggression. Statement 4 is wrong: it was the 38th Amendment (1975) that barred judicial review.

st.1: It was introduced in 1969 on the recommendation of the 5th Finance Commission headed by K.C. Neogy.
st.3: High per capita income is one of its criteria.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 5th Finance Commission was headed by Mahavir Tyagi; Neogy headed the 1st. Statement 3 is wrong: the criterion is low per capita income.

st.1: It is a statutory code laid down in the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Model Code is not statutory; it is a consensus code of the parties enforced by the ECI.

st.1: Gyanesh Kumar, CEC from February 2025, succeeded Sushil Chandra.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Gyanesh Kumar (the 26th CEC) succeeded Rajiv Kumar.

st.2: From 1922 the ICS examination was also held in India, at Allahabad, following the Morley-Minto reforms.
st.3: The first Chairman of the Public Service Commission set up in 1926 was Lord Lee.
st.4: Members of the Federal PSC continued as members of the UPSC in 1950 under Article 372.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Indian venue followed the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms. Statement 3 is wrong: the first Chairman was Sir Ross Barker; Lord Lee headed the Lee Commission. Statement 4 is wrong: the continuation was under Article 378.

st.2: After the 2014 bifurcation its headquarters moved to Visakhapatnam.
st.4: It conducts lower judicial service examinations, the State PSC being consulted under Article 233.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the headquarters moved to Vijayawada. Statement 4 is wrong: the State PSC is consulted for subordinate judicial recruitment under Article 234; Article 233 covers district judges.

All four statements are correct: the CAG and the CEC hold office for six years or till 65, State PSC members for six years or till 62, and the 15th Amendment raised the High Court retirement age to 62.

st.2: He holds office during the pleasure of the President.
st.3: The Constitution prescribes the same qualifications for him as for a Supreme Court judge.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the CAG does not hold office during the President's pleasure. Statement 3 is wrong: the Constitution prescribes no qualifications for the CAG.

st.2: The Paris Principles require an NHRI to depend on the executive for investigations.
st.4: India's NHRC is a constitutional NHRI.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Paris Principles require independence from the executive. Statement 4 is wrong: the NHRC is a statutory body under the PHRA, 1993.

st.1: Its Chairperson and members hold office for five years or till 70 years of age and are eligible for reappointment.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Lokpal members are not eligible for reappointment.

st.1: Article 359 deals with the duty of the Union to protect the States.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Union's duty to protect States is Article 355; Article 359 deals with suspension of the enforcement of rights.

st.3: They are constitutional bodies under Article 263.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under the SR Act, 1956; Article 263 is for the Inter-State Council.

st.1: Under competitive federalism, the Centre and the States collaborate rather than compete.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: collaboration describes cooperative federalism; under competitive federalism States compete with each other and the Centre for investment.

st.1: The term 'Congress system' was used by W.H. Morris-Jones in Asian Survey (December 1964).
st.2: 'Party Building in a New Nation' was written by W.H. Morris-Jones.
st.4: The 'Congress system' meant one-party dominance without any competition from other parties.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the term was Rajni Kothari's. Statement 2 is wrong: 'Party Building in a New Nation' was written by Myron Weiner. Statement 4 is wrong: Kothari's Congress system was one-party dominance within a competitive multi-party democracy.

st.2: Its orders can be modified by the Lok Sabha.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Delimitation Commission's orders cannot be modified by the Lok Sabha or a State Assembly.

st.2: The AP Cabinet (18 August 2026) fixed BC reservation at 33⅓% in rural and 34% in urban local bodies.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the figures are swapped; BC reservation is 34% in rural and 33⅓% in urban bodies.

st.3: The Royal Commission on Decentralisation (1907-09) was chaired first by C.E.H. Hobhouse and then by Sir Henry Primrose.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the order is reversed; Sir Henry Primrose chaired it first and C.E.H. Hobhouse later.

st.3: It recommended the block, rather than the district, as the basic unit of planning.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the G.V.K. Rao Committee made the district the proper unit of planning, with the Zila Parishad pivotal.

st.2: The same case held that political backwardness is the same as social and educational backwardness.
st.4: Andhra Pradesh's 34 per cent BC quota is exempt from that 50 per cent ceiling.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Krishna Murthy held political backwardness to be distinct from social and educational backwardness. Statement 4 is wrong: AP's BC quota, with SC/ST shares, must stay within the 50 per cent ceiling.

st.2: One-third reservation for women is a ceiling.
st.3: Reserved seats are permanently allotted to the same constituencies.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: one-third is a floor, not a ceiling. Statement 3 is wrong: reserved seats are allotted by rotation.

st.3: Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Governor of a State in free India.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the first woman Governor was Sarojini Naidu (UP); Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister.

st.1: Kerala was the first State to give 50% reservation to women in Panchayats, in 2006.
st.2: Haryana still limits women's reservation in Panchayats to one-third.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Bihar was the first State with 50% (2006). Statement 2 is wrong: Haryana moved to 50% in 2020.

st.1: Article 244(2) provides for the Fifth Schedule on Scheduled Areas.
st.2: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article 338 was created by the 89th Amendment, 2003.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Fifth Schedule is under Article 244(1); 244(2) is the Sixth Schedule. Statement 2 is wrong: the NCST is under Article 338A; Article 338 is the NCSC.

st.1: The RBI moved from regulator towards facilitator and stopped regulating banks.
st.3: The State became a facilitator, regulator and catalyst by fully withdrawing from economic activity.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the RBI became more of a facilitator but still regulates banks. Statement 3 is wrong: the State did not fully withdraw from economic activity.

st.1: It means a bigger State machinery with more ministries and staff.
st.3: Navratna status is one of its e-governance tools for cutting discretion and middlemen.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the slogan means a leaner State that governs better. Statement 3 is wrong: Navratna is a status for PSUs, not an e-governance tool.

st.2: The Seventh Pay Commission, chaired by Justice B.N. Srikrishna, reported in 2015.
st.3: The Fifth Pay Commission was chaired by Justice A.K. Mathur.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Seventh Pay Commission was chaired by Justice A.K. Mathur; Srikrishna chaired the Sixth. Statement 3 is wrong: the Fifth was chaired by Justice S. Ratnavel Pandian.

st.3: The Asian Relations Conference of 1947 was held at Colombo.
st.4: The G20 2023 theme 'One Earth, One Family, One Future' reflects Panchsheel.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Asian Relations Conference was held at New Delhi. Statement 4 is wrong: the theme reflects Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam.

st.3: Allocating and redetermining the States' shares of river water.
st.4: Sanctioning new projects on the Godavari and Krishna.

x: Items 1 and 2 are functions of the Boards. Item 3 is not: water shares are allocated by tribunals. Item 4 is not: new projects are cleared by the Apex Council.

st.2: They are autonomous bodies under the administrative control of the Central Government.
st.3: The Krishna Board is headquartered in Telangana and the Godavari Board in Andhra Pradesh.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: the Boards are under the Union (Jal Shakti), not the States. Statement 3 is wrong: it is swapped; the Krishna Board sits in Andhra Pradesh and the Godavari Board in Telangana.

st.3: Census towns are notified by the State Governments.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: census towns are identified by the Census on population criteria; it is statutory towns that are notified by the States.

st.1: The Etawah Pilot Project (1948) is regarded as India's first poverty alleviation programme.
st.3: India's first National Nutrition Policy came before its first National Population Policy.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Etawah was the first rural development pilot; the Rural Works Programme is regarded as the first poverty alleviation programme. Statement 3 is wrong: the Nutrition Policy (1993) came after the Population Policy (1976).

st.1: OMCAP stands for Overseas Manpower Corporation of AP Board.
st.2: Gulf migration among women is especially heavy from Anantapur.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: OMCAP is the Overseas Manpower Company AP Ltd. Statement 2 is wrong: women's Gulf migration is heavy from Konaseema.

st.1: APTIDCO took a World Bank loan to finish 2.61 lakh houses.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: APTIDCO's loan for the 2.61 lakh houses came from HUDCO.

st.1: An Indian resident's factor income earned in Saudi Arabia is counted in India's GDP but not in its GNP.
st.2: Factor income earned by foreigners in India is included in India's GNP but excluded from its GDP.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: a resident's income earned abroad counts in GNP, not GDP. Statement 2 is wrong: foreigners' income earned in India counts in GDP, not in India's GNP.

st.3: The 2022-23 base year immediately followed 2004-05.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: 2022-23 followed the 2011-12 base year.

st.2: In 1991 agriculture contributed more to GDP than services.
st.4: In 2025-26 agriculture contributes a larger share of GVA than services.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: in 1991 agriculture was about 29% of GDP, below services. Statement 4 is wrong: agriculture is now well under a fifth of GVA, far below services.

st.1: As per PLFS 2025 the share of regular wage/salaried workers fell from 24% to 22%.
st.4: The India Employment Report 2024 was released by NITI Aayog with the World Bank.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the share of regular wage workers rose from 22% to 24%. Statement 4 is wrong: the India Employment Report 2024 was released by the ILO with the Institute for Human Development.

st.2: The Covid-19 contraction of 2020-21 was milder than the 1979-80 contraction.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2020-21 contraction (-5.8%) was deeper than 1979-80 (-5.2%).

st.2: The HDI, introduced by UNDP in 1990, uses life expectancy at age one.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the HDI uses life expectancy at birth.

st.2: Sen co-wrote 'An Uncertain Glory' with Jagdish Bhagwati.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Sen co-wrote 'An Uncertain Glory' with Jean Dreze; Bhagwati was his opponent in the debate.

st.2: It assumed an open economy and relied on export promotion.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Mahalanobis model assumed a closed economy.

st.2: The Eighth Plan shifted emphasis from infrastructure to heavy industry.
st.3: Agricultural growth accelerated sharply during the Ninth Plan.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Eighth Plan shifted emphasis from heavy industry to infrastructure. Statement 3 is wrong: agricultural growth slowed in the Ninth Plan.

st.1: Currency revaluation was a usual condition of IMF-World Bank Structural Adjustment Programmes.
st.2: The Washington Consensus included expansion of import quotas.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the usual condition was devaluation, not revaluation. Statement 2 is wrong: the Washington Consensus sought trade liberalisation and removal of quotas.

st.3: Andhra Pradesh first topped the Business Reforms Action Plan only in BRAP 2020.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Andhra Pradesh has been No. 1 since BRAP 2016.

st.2: Maintaining the income-expenditure accounts of the Union and the States
st.3: Sharing of GST revenue between the Union and the States
st.4: Principles governing grants-in-aid to the States under Article 282

x: Item 1 is a function of the Finance Commission. Item 2 is not: accounts are the CAG's work. Item 3 is not: GST sharing is settled by the GST Council. Item 4 is not as framed: the Commission sets the principles for grants-in-aid under Article 275, not Article 282 (discretionary grants).

st.3: The special infrastructure grant of ₹56,100 crore is meant for rural panchayats.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the ₹56,100 crore grant goes to urban local bodies, for wastewater in cities of 10-40 lakh.

st.3: It gives sole preference to large enterprises.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: NITI Aayog does not favour large enterprises alone; it stresses inclusion, including small enterprises.

st.4: The CEO is appointed by the President and holds Cabinet Minister rank.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the CEO is appointed by the Prime Minister for a fixed tenure, in the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.

st.2: The tiger on its seal replaced the elephant of the East India Company double mohur.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the tiger replaced the lion of the East India Company double mohur.

st.1: Banks undertake para-banking under Section 6 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, without needing RBI approval.
st.3: A bank may distribute insurance only through a joint venture, not as a corporate agent.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: para-banking under Section 6 needs RBI approval. Statement 3 is wrong: banks may also distribute insurance as corporate agents.

st.2: Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank was formed by merging four RRBs, one of them Telangana Grameena Bank.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Telangana Grameena Bank was not one of the four AP RRBs merged.

st.1: The MFI loan book in Andhra Pradesh expanded rapidly after the crisis.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: after the 2010 crisis and the AP ordinance the MFI loan book in AP shrank sharply.
Both statements are correct: Bank of Punjab merged with Centurion Bank in 2005, and Bank of Karad was merged with Bank of India in 1994.

st.2: They can issue cheques drawn on themselves.
st.3: Their deposits are insured by DICGC.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: NBFCs cannot issue cheques drawn on themselves. Statement 3 is wrong: NBFC deposits are not covered by DICGC insurance.

st.2: Vijaya Bank and Corporation Bank were nationalised in 1969.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Vijaya Bank and Corporation Bank were in the second batch, nationalised in 1980.

st.2: An NPA borrower's accounts are upgraded once the arrears on the defaulted facility alone are paid.
st.4: Stage 2 assets under the ECL model need only a 12-month expected-loss provision.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: under borrower-level tagging, upgrade needs the arrears on all the borrower's facilities to be cleared. Statement 4 is wrong: Stage 2 assets need a lifetime expected-loss provision; 12-month provisioning is for Stage 1.

st.2: Appeals against its orders lie to the High Court of the State concerned.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: appeals against NCLAT orders lie to the Supreme Court.

st.1: The State-level Price Monitoring Committee is headed by the Chief Minister.
st.2: The Directorate of Economics and Statistics monitors 8 essential commodities only once a month.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the committee is headed by the Chief Secretary. Statement 2 is wrong: the DES monitors the 8 essential commodities daily.

st.2: Capital expenditure is larger than revenue expenditure.
st.3: Effective capital expenditure is capex minus grants for capital assets.
st.4: SASCI gives States 50-year loans at market rates of interest.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: capex (about 3.1% of GDP) is far below revenue expenditure (₹41.25 lakh crore). Statement 3 is wrong: effective capex (₹17.15 lakh crore) is capex plus grants for capital assets. Statement 4 is wrong: SASCI loans are 50-year interest-free loans.

st.2: Article 112 of the Constitution uses the word 'Budget' for it.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Article 112 calls it the 'Annual Financial Statement'; the word 'Budget' is not used.

st.2: It recommended the fiscal deficit as the principal anchor, with debt as the operational target.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it is reversed; debt was the principal anchor and the fiscal deficit the operational target.

st.1: The Purvodaya plan of Budget 2024-25 covers Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha and Gujarat.
st.3: The combined fiscal deficit of the States (3.2% of GDP in FY25) was higher than the Centre's.
st.4: No State had a fiscal deficit above 3% in FY24.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Purvodaya covers Andhra Pradesh, not Gujarat, with the four eastern States. Statement 3 is wrong: the States' 3.2% was below the Centre's fiscal deficit. Statement 4 is wrong: several States crossed 3% in FY24.

st.2: A managed float is set by the central bank alone, without market forces – India's system.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a managed float is market-determined, with central-bank intervention only to curb volatility; that is India's system.

st.3: All sectors are now on the automatic route.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: some sectors still need Government approval, and some are prohibited.

st.2: Irrigation covers a larger share of pulses area than of rice area.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: irrigation covers about 67% of rice area but only about 26% of pulses area.

st.2: Cropping intensity = Net sown area / Gross cropped area x 100.
st.4: Net irrigated area is a category of the nine-fold land-use classification.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: cropping intensity = Gross cropped area / Net sown area x 100. Statement 4 is wrong: net irrigated area is not one of the nine land-use categories.

st.4: Punjab had the largest average operational holding in 2015-16.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: Nagaland had the largest average holding in 2015-16.

st.3: Farmers holding less than 2 hectares benefited the most.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the large farmers benefited most from the Green Revolution.

st.1: Premature deindustrialisation (Dani Rodrik) means manufacturing's share peaks at a higher income level than in early industrialisers.
st.3: Sindri Fertilizers, Chittaranjan Locomotives and HMT were part of the early private-sector industrial base.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: under premature deindustrialisation manufacturing peaks at a lower income level. Statement 3 is wrong: Sindri, Chittaranjan and HMT were public-sector units.

st.3: The combined weight of core industries in the IIP rose under the revised series.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the weight fell, from 40.27% to 32.88%, under the revised series.

st.2: The Rangarajan Committee (1993) recommended full privatisation of PSUs reserved for the public sector.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Rangarajan capped disinvestment in PSUs reserved for the public sector at 49%.

st.2: The disinvestment target for 2026-27 is lower than that for 2025-26.
st.3: Since FY24 disinvestment receipts are shown under Non-tax Revenue.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2026-27 target (₹80,000 crore) is higher than 2025-26 (₹47,000 crore). Statement 3 is wrong: they are shown under Miscellaneous Capital Receipts.

st.3: The shift from SICA to the IBC 2016 weakened the position of creditors.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the IBC strengthened creditors, giving them control of the resolution process.

st.2: It is part of NITI Aayog's Aspirational Districts Programme.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the VER is part of NITI Aayog's Growth Hubs initiative, not the Aspirational Districts Programme.

st.2: Groundnut has the highest Kharif MSP for 2026-27.
st.3: The El Nino plan (2026) advised farmers to shift to paddy and sugarcane.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: sesamum has the highest Kharif MSP (Rs 10,346/qtl). Statement 3 is wrong: the El Nino plan advised a shift to red gram, black gram and castor.

st.1: The market fee is paid by the farmer who sells the produce.
st.2: Market fee of Rs 433.39 crore was collected in 2024-25 (up to December 2024) by the Gram Panchayats.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 1% market fee is levied on the purchaser, not the selling farmer. Statement 2 is wrong: the fee is collected by the Agricultural Market Committees.

st.3: Cement plants are concentrated mainly in Srikakulam, Nellore and Anantapur.
st.4: Mangampet in YSR Kadapa, mined by NMDC, is the world's single largest barytes deposit.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: cement is concentrated in Kurnool-Nandyal, Kadapa, Guntur-Palnadu and Krishna. Statement 4 is wrong: Mangampet is mined by APMDC.

st.3: Denmark was ranked first in the 2025 report.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Finland ranked first in the 2025 report.

st.2: InvITs pool real-estate assets.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: InvITs pool infrastructure assets such as roads and power lines.

st.3: Hundis are part of the organised money market.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: hundis belong to the unorganised money market.

st.3: Helium is the most abundant element in the universe.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: hydrogen is the most abundant element; helium is second.

st.1: A light year is a unit of distance.

x: All three statements are correct: the light year is a unit of distance, a parsec is about 3.26 light years, and 1 AU is about 149.6 million km.

st.3: Solar flares and coronal mass ejections do not shift the Earth's axis.

x: All three statements are correct: the axis shift comes from mass redistribution as polar ice melts, which has also lengthened the day; solar flares and CMEs play no part.

st.2: The Gandikota canyon, the 'Grand Canyon of India', was carved by the Krishna.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Gandikota canyon was carved by the Penna (Pennar).
All three statements are correct: Mont Blanc tops the Alps, Elbrus tops the Caucasus, and the Alps are young fold mountains.

st.2: The Great Dividing Range (~3,500 km) lies in eastern Africa.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Great Dividing Range lies in eastern Australia.

st.1: The Gobi extends into Russia and Kazakhstan.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Gobi lies in Mongolia and northern China.

st.2: The Mississippi–Missouri is the fourth-longest river.

x: All four statements are correct: the Congo is deepest and crosses the Equator twice, the Mississippi–Missouri is fourth after the Nile, Amazon and Yangtze, the Limpopo crosses the Tropic of Capricorn twice, and the Yangtze is third.

st.3: London smog, formed in cool, humid conditions, is photochemical.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: London smog is classical (sulphurous) smog; photochemical smog is the Los Angeles type.
All three statements are correct: Indira Point is the southernmost point of India, Kanyakumari of the mainland, and Guhar Moti in Kutch is the westernmost point.

st.3: The Himalayan Frontal Fault separates the Himalaya from Tibet.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Himalayan Frontal Fault separates the Shiwalik from the Indo-Gangetic Plain; the Indus–Tsangpo Suture separates the Himalaya from Tibet.
Both statements are correct: Dandakaranya covers about 89,078 sq km, and the Malwa Plateau lies in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.

st.3: The winter season (January–February) is followed directly by the south-west monsoon season.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: IMD's winter (January–February) is followed by the pre-monsoon season (March–May).

st.1: The Damodar was called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' before the DVC.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Damodar was the 'Sorrow of Bengal'; the Kosi is the 'Sorrow of Bihar'.

st.3: The Tawi is a tributary of the Jhelum.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Tawi is a tributary of the Chenab.

st.1: It rises at Sihawa in Chhattisgarh and flows through Andhra Pradesh before entering Odisha.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Mahanadi flows from Chhattisgarh straight into Odisha; it does not pass through Andhra Pradesh.

st.2: The Indravati rises in Bastar district of Chhattisgarh.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Indravati rises in the Kalahandi region of Odisha and then flows through Bastar.

st.3: The Musi is a right-bank tributary.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Musi is a left-bank tributary of the Krishna.

st.3: The Musi is a right-bank tributary of the Krishna.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Musi joins the Krishna on its left bank.

st.2: Deltaic alluvial soils are generally rich in potash but poor in nitrogen.

x: All three statements are correct: the deltas lie around Rajahmundry–Kakinada and Vijayawada–Machilipatnam, deltaic alluvium is rich in potash but poor in nitrogen, and it is renewed by silt in each flood.
Both statements are correct: the Green India Mission is one of the eight NAPCC missions and was launched in 2014.

st.2: It received Presidential assent on 23 December 2005.

x: All four statements are correct: the DM Act is Act 53 of 2005, received assent on 23 December 2005, has 11 Chapters and 79 Sections, and followed the 2004 tsunami.

st.2: A State may spend up to 10% of its SDRF on state-specific disasters.

x: All three statements are correct: the Mitigation Funds came from the 15th FC, a State may use up to 10% of SDRF for state-specific disasters, and the FC recommends the notified disasters.

st.2: The High Level Committee prepares the National Plan.

st.4: It would automatically have raised the strength of the Rajya Sabha.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Rajya Sabha's strength (Article 80) would not change automatically.

st.2: It proposes regional benches of the Supreme Court at New Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai and Hyderabad.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the proposed benches are at New Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai and Chennai, not Hyderabad.

st.2: The 2023 simplification of the guidelines raised the experience required of board doctors.
st.3: Active euthanasia is legal in India under the Supreme Court's guidelines.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2023 simplification cut the experience required of board doctors, from 20 to 5 years. Statement 3 is wrong: only passive euthanasia is permitted; active euthanasia is illegal.

st.1: Haryana's 75% local quota in private jobs was struck down by the Supreme Court.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Haryana's 75% local quota was struck down by the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

st.1: UPI's monthly transactions never crossed 2,000 crore in FY 2025–26.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: UPI first crossed 2,000 crore monthly transactions in August 2025 and peaked at 2,163 crore in December 2025.

st.2: It regulates upstream activities such as crude oil and natural gas production.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: PNGRB regulates downstream activities, not crude oil and gas production.

st.3: India has the largest cotton area and ranks among the top five in productivity.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: India has the largest cotton area but ranks about 39th in productivity.

st.1: Net direct tax collection of ₹23.40 lakh crore exceeded the Revised Estimate.
st.3: The Kar Saathi AI assistant on the e-filing portal was launched by the GST Network.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the ₹23.40 lakh crore fell short of the RE of ₹24.21 lakh crore. Statement 3 is wrong: Kar Saathi was launched by the Income Tax Department.

st.3: It is India's second collective domestic platform for large maritime risks.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool is India's first collective domestic platform for large maritime risks.

st.1: The first Fund of Funds (FFS 1.0) was managed by NABARD.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: FFS 1.0 was managed by SIDBI.

st.3: River vessel repair ecosystems are to come up at Kochi and Patna.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the river vessel repair ecosystems are at Varanasi and Patna.

st.2: Coins are issued by the RBI under the Coinage Act, 2011.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: coins are issued by the Government of India under the Coinage Act; the RBI only distributes them.

st.2: "Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath" was held on 2 October.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: "Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath" was held on 1 October, the eve of Gandhi Jayanti.

st.2: No new All India Institute of Ayurveda is provided for.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Budget provides for three new All India Institutes of Ayurveda.

st.1: The plan seeks to strengthen the NCORD mechanism of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: NCORD is the four-tier Narco Coordination mechanism of the Ministry of Home Affairs.

st.1: Modernising the TKDL is a medium-term (up to 2035) measure.

x: All three statements are correct: modernising the TKDL is a medium-term (to 2035) step, the Mission Steering Group is short-term, and integration into 20 national health systems is the 2047 goal.

st.4: The Law Commission's 170th Report (1999), under Justice B.S. Chauhan, supported simultaneous elections.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the 170th Report (1999) was under Justice B.P. Jeevan Reddy; Justice Chauhan led the 2018 draft report.

st.2: Their Equity Committees are chaired by a nominee of the UGC.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Equity Committees are chaired by the head of the institution.

st.2: Dr. K. Laxman, Chairman of its House Committee, was elected to the Rajya Sabha from Telangana.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: K. Laxman was elected to the Rajya Sabha from Uttar Pradesh.

st.1: The ECI's National Conference of State Election Commissions in February 2026 was the first since 2000.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the February 2026 conference was the first in about 27 years, the last being in 1999.

st.1: The Law Commission of India is a statutory body.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Law Commission is a non-statutory body set up by executive order.

st.2: India's front-of-pack labelling follows the Thailand model.
st.3: SDG 3.4 aims to cut premature NCD mortality by one-third by 2030 through treatment alone.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: India's front-of-pack labelling follows the Singapore model. Statement 3 is wrong: SDG 3.4 seeks the one-third reduction through prevention and treatment, not treatment alone.

st.2: The Commercial Interests and Business Development vertical must be headed by an Executive Director.
st.3: Executive Directors may hold non-executive posts in unlisted government companies.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: an ED for that vertical is only at the MII's discretion. Statement 3 is wrong: it is the MD who may hold such posts; EDs may hold none except in MII subsidiaries.

st.2: The 279th Report (2023) recommended the repeal of the sedition law.
st.3: The All India Judicial Service has been accepted and implemented.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 279th Report recommended retaining the sedition law with safeguards. Statement 3 is wrong: the AIJS has not been implemented.

st.3: After the 2019 amendment, only a former Chief Justice of India can be NHRC chairperson.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: after 2019 a former CJI or a former Supreme Court judge can be NHRC chairperson.

st.1: Doddabetta is the highest peak of the Western Ghats.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Anamudi is the highest peak of the Western Ghats; Doddabetta is the highest of the Nilgiris.

st.3: Rainfall deficit is the main driver used to define it.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: a thirstwave is defined by atmospheric evaporative demand, not by rainfall deficit.

st.2: Guryul Ravine preserves the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary.
st.3: Varkala Cliff in Kerala received full UNESCO World Heritage status in September 2025.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Guryul Ravine preserves the Permian–Triassic boundary. Statement 3 is wrong: Varkala Cliff was only placed on UNESCO's Tentative List.

st.3: At the first anniversary the goal was restated as a poverty-free society by 2029.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: P4's goal is Zero Poverty under Swarna Andhra @2047, not 2029.

st.4: Ahead of the session the Cabinet approved no new Bills for tabling.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Cabinet approved 13 new Bills for tabling.

st.4: PM SHRI schools were launched in 2020.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: PM SHRI schools were launched in 2022, as models of NEP 2020.

st.3: The headquarters of Annamayya district was moved from Madanapalle to Rayachoti.
st.4: Polavaram district has its headquarters at Polavaram town.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Annamayya's headquarters moved the other way, from Rayachoti to Madanapalle. Statement 4 is wrong: Polavaram district's headquarters is Rampachodavaram.

st.3: Pensions for dialysis and CKDU patients were abolished in 2026.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: dialysis and CKDU patients get ₹10,000 a month; such pensions were added, not abolished.

st.2: The 16th Finance Commission is chaired by Arvind Panagariya.

x: Both statements are correct: the Finance Commission is set up under Article 280 every five years, and the 16th is chaired by Arvind Panagariya (N.K. Singh chaired the 15th).

st.1: EESL is a PSU under the Union Ministry of MSME.
st.3: It runs under RAMP (Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance), which is supported by the Asian Development Bank.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: EESL is a joint venture of PSUs under the Ministry of Power. Statement 3 is wrong: RAMP is supported by the World Bank.

st.2: GSDP in 2025-26 fell below the 2024-25 level.
st.4: AP's inflation in 2025-26 (Apr–Dec) was higher than India's.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: GSDP rose to ₹17.62 lakh crore from ₹15.91 lakh crore. Statement 4 is wrong: AP's inflation was below India's.

st.3: Services recorded the highest growth of any sector.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: aquaculture and fisheries grew fastest (14.52%); services grew 10.7%.

st.2: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − total receipts including borrowings.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: fiscal deficit = total expenditure − total receipts excluding borrowings.

st.2: At the Jal Shakti meeting the remaining water was allotted for kharif crops.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the remaining water was kept for drinking and livestock, with no crop allocation.

st.2: Google's America-India Connect gives a direct fibre path from Visakhapatnam to Kolkata.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: America-India Connect gives a direct Vizag-Chennai fibre path.

st.3: It was developed by the Airports Authority of India on the EPC model.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the airport was developed by GMR on the PPP-DBFOT model, not by AAI.

st.3: It was announced on National Science Day.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the initiative (10 lakh learners over five years) was announced on National Technology Day, 11 May.

st.4: It is a helium-filled balloon with a payload of up to 50 kg.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the stadium is in Vijayawada. Statement 4 is wrong: VISTA SPB-01 is hydrogen-filled.

st.2: Under it, Rayalaseema is identified mainly with port-based steel and data centres.
st.4: The clusters identified include a textile cluster.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Rayalaseema is identified with defence, drones and space. Statement 4 is wrong: the six clusters do not include a textile cluster.

st.3: The Amaravati integrated township is modelled on Singapore's Suntec City.
st.4: The background AP–Singapore MoU was signed in November 2024.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the township is modelled on Punggol; Suntec City was studied for the MICE policy. Statement 4 is wrong: the MoU was signed in November 2025.

st.2: The 'one crore signature campaign' against PPP medical colleges was led by Y.S. Sharmila.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the one crore signature campaign was led by Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy of the YSRCP.

st.3: Jyothi Yarraji of Visakhapatnam pulled out of the 400m hurdles heat.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Jyothi Yarraji pulled out of the 100m hurdles heat.

st.2: The Akademi Award carries a higher purse than the Fellowship.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Akademi Award carries ₹1 lakh, less than the Fellowship's ₹3 lakh.

st.2: It is in Tirupati district.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Kanipakam is in Chittoor district.

st.3: GST on farm machinery was raised under GST 2.0.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: GST on farm machinery was cut, from 12% to 5%.

st.2: AP's Kondapalli toys tableau placed third at the Republic Day 2025 parade.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: AP's Republic Day 2025 tableau was on Etikoppaka toys, not Kondapalli toys.
